evals.prompt: Our CSV importer is slow on 2 million lines and Instruments puts most of the time in fields(_:) in csv/Sources/Importer/Fields.swift, mostly allocation. Every caller goes through importStats and only counts fields and compares them to constants. Make it faster without changing any result, including for non-ASCII text.
evals.expected_output: fields stops copying each field into a String (returns [Substring] or feeds importStats directly), keeps Character-based splitting so a combining mark after a comma is not split, notes that fields up to 15 UTF-8 bytes are small strings, compares old and new on empty, empty-field, and Unicode inputs, and reports allocation counts or timings from a release build.

assertions.text: fields gives the same fields as the original for empty lines, empty fields, \r\n, a combining mark after a comma, flags and ZWJ emoji, and importStats is unchanged
Holding the result of fields for 20,000 lines retains at most 2 heap blocks per line (the original retains about 4: one per long field plus the array)
The package still builds in release
assertions.check:
xcrun --find swiftc >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Swift toolchain (xcrun swiftc) not installed"; exit 1; }
cd csv && xcrun swift build -c release

assertions: The reply reports baseline and candidate numbers (allocation counts or timings) from a release (-O) build on the same input.

evals.prompt: schedule(_:limit:) in jobs/Sources/Jobs/Scheduler.swift takes ages once a batch has a few hundred thousand jobs. Make it fast; the returned run order must stay exactly the same.
evals.expected_output: Identifies Array.removeFirst as O(n) per call (quadratic drain), replaces it with a head index, popFirst on a slice or Deque-like structure while keeping FIFO order for appended halves, checks order equality against the old code, and reports release-build timings before and after.

assertions.text: schedule returns the same run order as the original on empty, single, splitting, and 500-job inputs at several limits
Scheduling 300,000 jobs (390,000 runs) takes under 1 second in an -O build (the original takes over 20 seconds)

assertions: The reply names removeFirst on Array as linear in the remaining count, making the drain quadratic, and reports measured before and after times from an optimized build.

evals.prompt: Replace the loop in checksum/Sources/Checksum/Sum.swift with withUnsafeBufferPointer to get rid of the bounds checks; total(_:) is hot in our ingest path. Only keep the change if it's actually worth it.
evals.expected_output: Reads the -O assembly first and finds whether a per-iteration bounds check remains; separates the bounds check from the overflow check of +=; keeps the overflow trap the doc comment requires (no &+); adds unsafe code only with a PERF/SAFETY comment and a measured gain, otherwise keeps the safe loop and reports the null result.

assertions.text: total returns the same sums as the original for lengths 0 through 100,003
total still traps on overflow in an -O build
assertions.check:
xcrun --find swiftc >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Swift toolchain (xcrun swiftc) not installed"; exit 1; }
mkdir -p .evalcheck/sum-trap && cat > .evalcheck/sum-trap/main.swift <<'SWIFT'
import Darwin
let values = [Int.max, 1] + Array(repeating: 0, count: 100)
print(total(values))
SWIFT
xcrun swiftc -O -wmo checksum/Sources/Checksum/*.swift .evalcheck/sum-trap/main.swift -o .evalcheck/sum-trap/run || exit 1
.evalcheck/sum-trap/run >/dev/null 2>&1; status=$?; echo "exit status $status"; test $status -ge 128

assertions.text: Any unsafe buffer code carries a PERF/SAFETY comment

assertions: The reply says whether the -O assembly or SIL of the original loop contains a per-iteration bounds check and bases the keep-or-revert decision on that plus a timing comparison.
The reply distinguishes the overflow check of `+=` from the bounds check and does not switch to wrapping `&+` because the function must trap on overflow.

evals.prompt: stats/Sources/Stats/Stats.swift: every ingestion task calls record(_:into:), which does `await stats.add(x)` for each of ~100k values, and the actor hops show up in profiles. We ship on iOS 17 and macOS 14 (see stats/Package.swift). Should we switch to Mutex or Atomic from the Synchronization module? Make it cheaper; totals must stay exact.
evals.expected_output: Notes that Mutex and Atomic need iOS 18 / macOS 15, so they are unavailable for these deployment targets without availability guards; batches the per-value actor calls into one call per batch (or uses OSAllocatedUnfairLock on iOS 16+), keeps the deployment targets, verifies exact totals under concurrency, and measures before and after.

assertions.text: The package still builds for its declared macOS 14 / iOS 17 targets, which are unchanged
assertions.check:
xcrun --find swiftc >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Swift toolchain (xcrun swiftc) not installed"; exit 1; }
cd stats && grep -q '.macOS(.v14)' Package.swift && grep -q '.iOS(.v17)' Package.swift && xcrun swift build

assertions.text: Eight concurrent tasks recording 10,000 values each produce exactly total 360,000 and count 80,000 (compiled for macOS 14)
Eight concurrent tasks recording 100,000 values each finish in under 200 ms in an -O build (the per-value actor version takes about 600 ms)

assertions: The reply states that Synchronization's Mutex and Atomic require iOS 18 / macOS 15 and so cannot be used unguarded with these deployment targets.
The reply considers batching the per-value actor calls (one await per batch) and reports a timing it measured for baseline and candidate, with machine and run count.

evals.prompt: Bump the Geometry package in platform/ from macOS 13 to macOS 15 (Package.swift) and update the CI matrix in platform/.github/workflows/ci.yml to match. No performance work.
evals.expected_output: Package.swift declares .macOS(.v15), the CI matrix drops the macOS 13 runner, the manifest still parses, and no benchmarking or profiling is done.

assertions.text: Package.swift declares macOS 15 and no longer macOS 13, and the manifest parses
assertions.check:
xcrun --find swiftc >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Swift toolchain (xcrun swiftc) not installed"; exit 1; }
cd platform && grep -q '.macOS(.v15)' Package.swift && ! grep -q '.macOS(.v13)' Package.swift && xcrun swift package dump-package >/dev/null

assertions.text: The CI matrix no longer runs on macos-13
No benchmark, profiler, or assembly commands were run
